🥺 ChatGPT faces another major lawsuit over medical advice

OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman are being sued after a U.S. pastor claimed ChatGPT downplayed symptoms of a life-threatening pulmonary embolism and discouraged him from seeking medical care.

The lawsuit argues ChatGPT crossed into practicing medicine without a license and calls for its health features to be suspended until they’re independently verified as safe.

OpenAI says ChatGPT isn’t meant to diagnose or treat medical conditions, but the case adds to growing legal scrutiny over the chatbot’s health advice.

🤖 Altman to Present New OpenAI Model in DC

Sam Altman is heading to Washington to show the White House a new internal OpenAI model. This is likely the same model that leaked into Hugging Face's environment.

The model is pitched as capable of solving long-standing math problems and making complex business tasks cheaper and more efficient for US companies.

🗣 Sam Altman reveals he flew to 28 countries in 35 days after GPT-4 launched because world leaders were asking whether to shut AI down, and ended the trip waking up convinced he was back in his childhood bed.

“Three years ago we had just launched GPT-4. The world was melting down. Everybody was freaking out.”

“World leaders were like, do we need to take control and shut things down? Is this thing waking up?”

“I think we did 28 countries, 35 days. I lived on an airplane.”

“By the end of it, the last few days, I started having this vision, feeling, whatever, of being in my childhood bed. I would sort of vaguely wake up and I would think I was in my childhood bed in my childhood room. And I was like, okay, this is some deep ‘it’s time to go home’ thing.”
